Informational page with facts and a construction photo. No pieces are placed, so all 22 parts-list lines are still unplaced.

Step 1: two Plate 4x10 are placed side by side along their long edges, forming an 8x10 base. They only touch edge to edge, so b2 does not clutch b1 from below. The rests_on link b2 -> b1 is the closest the format allows, so b2 should be treated as side by side with b1.

Step 2: four 1x8 tiles go around the edge of the base. Two sit on the short ends and span both plates. The other two run along the long sides, one on each plate, leaving a 6x8 stud area in the middle.
I assumed the printed 'John Hancock Center' tile (b6) is on the front long side, resting on b2. Which plate is the front one is a guess. The other long-side tile b5 rests on b1.
The three plain tiles are the three lego-4162 from the parts list. The printed tile makes the fourth.
Step 3: two Plate 4x6 in light bluish gray sit side by side in the 6x8 well inside the black tile border. Each spans both base plates (b1 and b2), because the base seam runs along the long axis.

Step 4: four Tile 1x6 form a frame on the grey plates. Two sit at the short ends, one on each grey plate. The other two run along the long sides and span both grey plates. This leaves a 4x6 stud area in the middle. The arrows show one of the long-side tiles going on; I assumed the other three tiles sit in the same frame.
b7 and b8 are the left and right grey plates. Which one is which is a guess. They are interchangeable.

Step 5: two Tile 1x2 and one Plate 2x2, all black, go into the 6x4 well inside the grey tile frame. Step 6: eight jumper plates (1x2 with 1 stud) fill the rest. Together the 24 cells are covered: tiles 4, plate 4, jumpers 16.

The exact positions inside the well are hard to read from the small pictures. I assumed the tiles and the 2x2 plate sit over grey plate b7, and the jumpers cover the rest of b7 and all of b8. The rests_on lists follow that assumption.
Nothing here sits on the grey frame tiles (b9 to b12). They only surround the filled area.
Step 7: one Brick 2x3 and two Brick 1x3 form a first brick layer over the jumper plates, covering a 4x3 footprint on the grey plate b8 side. The 2x2 black plate (b15) is left exposed.
Step 8: two more Brick 2x3 go on top of that layer, and a light bluish grey Plate Round 2x2 with axle hole goes on the exposed 2x2 plate b15.

The rests_on lists for these bricks are my best guess. The pictures are small, so I could not tell which jumper plates are under each brick, or whether the upper bricks are offset from the lower ones. I assumed the top bricks line up with the bricks below.

Step 9: a black Plate Round 1x1 is pushed into the bottom of a light grey Plate Round 2x2 with axle hole. The pair is then put on top of the round plate b29. Step 10 repeats this: b32 and b33 go on top of b31.
Step 10 also adds a third brick layer to the tower: one Brick 2x3 and two Brick 1x3, which mirror the layout of step 7.
I took the 1x1 round plate to sit in the centre hole of the plate below it, so it is listed as resting on that lower plate, not on the new one. Its link to the new plate is in other_joins.
As on earlier pages, the rests_on lists for the new bricks follow my assumed layout. The pictures are too small to confirm it.

Step 11: a light bluish grey Tile Round 2x2 with bottom cross caps the round plate stack (b39 on b33). Two black Plate 2x3 are laid on the top brick layer of the tower. b37 covers b36, and b38 covers the two 1x3 bricks b34 and b35.
Step 12: a Tile 1x4 and four jumper plates (1x2 with 1 stud) cover the 4x3 top deck. The tile runs along one 4-stud edge, spanning both plates. The jumpers fill the rest, two on each plate.
Which edge the tile sits on is a guess. The pictures are too small to confirm it, so the rests_on lists here are best estimates.
Step 13: three Brick 2x4 are stacked, then a Plate 2x4 goes on top. This narrows the tower to a 2x4 footprint, as the real building tapers. Step 14: four jumper plates cover the Plate 2x4.
The first 2x4 brick (b45) sits on the four jumper plates of the previous step (b41 to b44). The Tile 1x4 b40 has no studs, so I assumed nothing clutches it. This is my reading of the pictures.
The tower layers are aligned, not staggered, as far as I can tell from the pictures.

Step 15: three Brick 2x3 are stacked on the four jumper plates (b49 to b52), then a Plate 2x3 goes on top. This narrows the tower again, to a 2x3 footprint. Step 16: three jumper plates cover the Plate 2x3.
The first brick (b53) is assumed to touch all four jumper plates below it. The tower layers are assumed aligned, not staggered.
Step 17: three Brick 1x3 are stacked on the three jumper plates (b57 to b59), narrowing the tower to a 1x3 footprint.
Step 18 is a small sub-assembly built in three inset steps. It is not attached to the tower on this page, so b63 rests on nothing yet. I assume it goes on top of the tower on the next page.

Sub-assembly: a white Plate 1x3 goes between two black Plate 1x3. A black Plate 1x1 and a Tile 1x1 are stacked on the middle stud. The two white antennas go on the end studs. The inset pictures are small, so I could not confirm that a black plate sits above the white one. It matches the two black Plate 1x3 on the parts list and the white stripe seen in the pictures. The antennas sit on the end studs on either side of the 1x1 stack.
After this page nothing is left on the parts list except what the sub-assembly used.

The arrow shows the antenna sub-assembly from page 12 going onto the top of the tower, so it attaches to the top 1x3 brick b62 through its bottom plate b63. It is listed in other_joins because b63 was recorded earlier with nothing under it.
The rest of the page is the finished model and a parts overview. No pieces are added.
